chapter: Hutto 1978-79: family, favorites and record lists
title: Buying old Specht records: the Paramount session
summary: Hutto reports a collector has Specht and Georgians records at $3 each; Morehouse says he was New York's number one drummer and recorded for Paramount.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay and I mentioned on the phone that I had contacted this man who has old records, that I've gotten records from him. And I went over there Saturday. And he has a number of Paul Specht records and a number of the Georgian records.
And they are $3 a piece. So I thought maybe we could decide on if you wanted to get any or I want a few of them of course. And he said drop him a note and he will pick them out.
Well they were rather old-fashioned style.
Well let's call out some. If any of them strike your fancy, we'll make sure we get them. Now one of them, let's see...Apparently before you made records for Columbia, you made one for Paramount.
I used to get periodic Paramount,....
So definitely we want to get that. I think it's called Specht's Jazz Group or something like that. We'll see what that is.
Well I was the number one drummer in New York City and everybody would call me first. And if I didn't have a date, I would take it.
Get the right page here. Specht's Jazz Outfit, June 29, 1922. "You Can Have Him, I Don't Want Him Blues" and "Hot Lips".
He has the Puritan. Paramount has another subsidiary. So that he has the Puritan label. And we'll definitely get that one. So that's the first one.
